correctness.rationale: Kitajima's definition and Corollary 4.19 apply to precisely the proper Boolean rank-span complex and concentrate its reduced homology in degree k. A fixed simplex cannot permute vertices of different ranks, so it has trace +1. Its fixed vertices are whole-cycle unions. For a nonempty set J of cycles between the two endpoints the remaining cycles give 2^(c-|J|)-2 valid endpoint assignments, and the alternating sum over ordered nonempty increments is (-1)^|J| by the falling-factorial identity. Together with the reduced augmentation this gives the stated cycle product with the stated sign. Independently, cover by rank-selected windows W_i=[i,i+k], i=1,...,n-k-1. Each new window meets the previous union precisely in the rank-selected complex on [i,i+k-1], since any face in it already has rank at least i and the previous union has upper ranks at most i+k-1. Reduced Mayer–Vietoris and concentration of rank-selected Boolean homology show that the top module is the sum, up to rational isomorphism, of the ribbon modules of the windows (k+1 ranks) and the successive intersections (k ranks, i=2,...,n-k-1). Equivalently the signs in the equivariant reduced Euler characteristic give positive contributions for both. The standard exact-descent-set rule for these ribbons gives one hook per permitted descent set of the prescribed cardinality, since a standard tableau of hook leg r is uniquely specified by its r descents. This yields n-k-1 copies at leg k+1 and n-k-2 at leg k, and none for the trivial hook. This independently checks the endpoint case k=n-2, when only the full-rank sign module remains, and includes k=1. In the quotient, the rank span condition gives a rank complex in which the leftmost vertex link is a cone on its successor, confirming contractibility. The frozen code was inspected, not executed.

originality.rationale: Credit the previously known span-two character, nonequivariant persistence, Kitajima's window union and concentration, and the rank-selected ribbon representation theorem. Importantly, these last two primary papers together already give a direct route to the representation and the hook numbers via equivariant gluing. The distinct contribution supported here is the evaluated, uniform cycle-type trace formula for the whole range, with an explicit evaluation of the hook spectrum. It is not a new concentration, ribbon, or quotient theorem, and I do not credit the broader assertion that prior equivariant rank-selection theory cannot compute these filtered representations.

value.rationale: A short cycle-type formula gives trace values at every permutation in every moving-window stage without decomposing ribbon modules or enumerating fixed chains. It determines the rational action, not just dimensions or persistence. The evaluated two-hook support makes the representation-theoretic effect of the rank-span cutoff explicit, including the unique terminal appearance of sign. The value is in these natural evaluated invariants, not the mere substitution of rank sets into the known ribbon theorem.
